events.date_basis: FOMC statement released October 28 at 14:00 EDT (October 29 at 03:00 JST); Tokyo cash bond market had closed
events.title: FOMC holds 3.75-4.00% target range (10-2 vote)
events.summary: The FOMC maintained the federal funds target range at 3.75-4.00% on October 28 by a 10-2 vote; two members preferred a 25bp increase. This is U.S. policy context for JGB and yen monitoring, not a BoJ decision.
events.caveat: Official release is October 28 U.S. Eastern time; displayed on October 29, the first subsequent Tokyo session. Chart placement does not establish a causal JGB or yen response, or the size of any Fed surprise.

events.date_basis: Decision at October 29-30, 2026 MPM, dated October 30 in Japan; no intraday market timing inferred
events.title: BoJ maintains 1.25% overnight rate and increases ETF disposal pace
events.summary: At its October 30 MPM, the BoJ kept the uncollateralized overnight call rate around 1.25% by an 8-1 vote and unanimously raised the annual ETF sale pace from about JPY330bn to about JPY860bn on a book-value basis, to be implemented in January 2027.
events.classification: Policy-rate hold and faster planned ETF disposals
events.caveat: The ETF change was decided October 30, not implemented that day; the official statement specifies January 2027 without an exact day. No future rate decision, intraday market effect or realized ETF sale is inferred.

sources.title: Bank of Japan: Statement on Monetary Policy (October 30, 2026)
quotes: October 30, 2026
The Bank will encourage the uncollateralized overnight call rate to remain at around 1.25 percent.
and set the pace of sales at about 860 billion yen per year (on a book value basis).
The change will be implemented in January 2027.

events.title: Annual primary-balance target reconsidered
events.summary: Takaichi tells the House of Representatives Budget Committee that she intends to change the annual primary-balance approach and consider assessment over several years.
events.caveat: A stated change in approach, not abandonment of all fiscal discipline. The November 9 news report is later than this November 7 testimony. Earlier disclosure and surprise remain unverified.

quotes: 単年度のプライマリーバランスという考え方については変更する、取り下げると考えていただいて結構かと思います。

events.title: FY2026 budget enacted
events.summary: The FY2026 budget passes the House of Councillors and is enacted. This is the parliamentary stage of the budget previously shown at F21.
events.classification: Fiscal implementation milestone; no separate direction

events.date_basis: Dated official communication in Japan; first-public intraday time is unverified
events.title: Summer energy relief and supplementary-budget plan
events.summary: Takaichi announces July-September electricity and gas assistance requiring approximately JPY500bn, with reserve-fund approval planned the next day, and a supplementary budget exceeding JPY3tn. Reduced FY2025 bond issuance is intended to offset the additional financing in total market issuance.
events.caveat: Announcement stage preceding F23 (June 3 draft). Reserve-funded energy assistance and supplementary-budget reserves are different components and must not be added as independent packages. Spending capacity is not realized demand; no surprise is measured.

sources.title: Prime Minister: Middle East response and supplementary budget
quotes: approximately 500 billion yen
We expect the scale of the supplementary budget to be over three trillion yen.

events.title: Draft fiscal framework and investment-budget reforms
events.summary: The draft Basic Policy sets out a separate investment framework, steady debt-to-GDP reduction as the core fiscal-management target, and a longer-term economic and fiscal plan. Cabinet approval is sought for mid-July.
events.caveat: Draft stage linked to F24 (July 21 approval). Related investment-budget proposals were already discussed on June 25-26; June 30 is not certified as first disclosure. No spending total or market surprise is inferred.

sources.title: Prime Minister: Council on Economic and Fiscal Policy, June 30
quotes: Today we discussed the draft of the Basic Policy on Economic and Fiscal Management and Reform.

events.title: Retail JGB and domestic-asset investment proposals
events.summary: Katayama proposes improving retail JGB products and exploring support for further household and pension-fund investment in Japanese financial assets. July 14 follow-up discusses NISA eligibility and inheritance-tax ideas while acknowledging GPIF rules and consultation requirements.
events.caveat: July 10 proposal cluster with July 14 clarification. No adopted GPIF allocation change, instruction to purchase JGBs, NISA expansion or inheritance-tax change is established. Earlier proposals existed; first disclosure is unverified.
